name: heredity_module_comparison
description: A reusable heredity-module comparison (Module J). Genuine libRoadRunner quasispecies replicator (Eigen error threshold): a heredity module (RNA-like / peptide / low-fidelity / non-heritable) replicates a polymer with whole-sequence fidelity Q = fidelity^length; above the threshold the functional information is retained and inheritance pays, below it errors win. Compares modules head-to-head on lineage fitness. Requires tellurium/libroadrunner.

module.description: Heredity-module preset: rna-like | peptide | low-fidelity | non-heritable

herd_proc.doc:
Real libRoadRunner quasispecies replicator for the Eigen error threshold.
Reads temperature (Arrhenius on the replication rate); advances the genuine
SBML ODE each tick; and emits the information retention, functional template
level, polymer length and lineage fitness (overwrite sensors — the current
population state). A heredity MODULE is a (fidelity, length, rate, cost) set;
the non-heritable control sets krep=0.

_contract.summary: Real libRoadRunner quasispecies replicator (Eigen error threshold): does inherited polymer state improve fitness despite fidelity + cost? Heredity modules compared head-to-head.
_contract.description: Drives the genuine libRoadRunner integrator on a logistic quasispecies ODE (correct templates C vs mutational errors E; whole-sequence fidelity Q = per_site_fidelity^length). Emits information retention C/(C+E), the functional template level, polymer length and lineage fitness = benefit*(retention*C) - cost*krep. Above the error threshold the functional information is retained and inheritance pays; below it errors win (catastrophe). RNA-like (long, high-fidelity, costly) vs peptide-assisted (short, cheaper, lower-fidelity) are compared; krep=0 is the non-heritable control.
math: dC/dt = krep*Q*C*(1-(C+E)/K) - kdeg*C ;  dE/dt = krep*(1-Q)*C*(..) + krep*qe*E*(..) - kdeg*E
assumptions: Eigen quasispecies error threshold: whole-sequence fidelity Q = per_site_fidelity^length.
Logistic carrying capacity bounds growth; errors replicate with reduced fidelity qe.
Lineage fitness nets the retained functional throughput against the replication budget.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
